bounded_difference.bootstrap_degeneracy: percentile bootstrap collapses to [0,0] at m=0; the exact two-sided 95% upper bound at 0/24 is 0.1425 (equivalently one-sided 97.5%; the one-sided 95% bound is 0.1173), reported alongside so a degenerate interval is never read as equivalence
bounded_difference.does_not_rule_out: any difference inside [-0.0833, 0.2500], including zero and any band narrower than the interval
bounded_difference.identity_conflict_rule: identity must cover every measured unit whose candidate set holds one question (n_overlap >= n_expected, 0 mismatch). It is a precondition, not a competing criterion: the reading has no threshold, so the two cannot exclude each other.
bounded_difference.power_note: at n=24 one unit is 4.17 pp; with m discordant pairs the paired interval is about +-1.96*sqrt(m)/24, so the narrowest non-degenerate symmetric band is +-2 units at m=1 and +-4 units at m=3; a +-3-unit (0.125) band is not attainable together with a 24/24 identity re-execution.
bounded_difference.statement: bounded-difference statement only. No equivalence threshold, no pass/fail rule, and no 'sixteen frames answer as much as one frame' sentence.

coverage.rule: e_max = the largest e with e <= B(n_pairs - e, p_hi) (C = 0, the most favourable case); a cell with more than e_max unevaluable pairs cannot pass at any contradiction count.  required_coverage_frac = (n_pairs - e_max)/n_pairs.  slack_b_minus_c = B - C is the distance from the line at the observed n_eval; it is NOT how many further unevaluable pairs this run could absorb, because B shrinks with each one.  That quantity is max_absorbable_unevaluable_pairs = the largest e' with C + e' <= B(n_pairs - e', p_hi); quote that one for 'how many more the run could take'.  (This replaces the field `margin_pairs`, whose definition was B - C while its prose claimed the absorbable count.)

fault_injection.rule: the same comparison function that produces `mapping` is re-run with the letter->option index map deliberately offset (identity, +1, -1, and +1 on one parity). A criterion that derived the option text from the letter would be invariant to all four. `fired` is true only when the offset is caught on every pair it touches, the identity run reproduces the reported count, and the offset verdict is fail. identical_repeat.structurally_zero_note: a greedy decode repeated with the same prompt is bit-identical by construction, so this is a check that the naming decode path is deterministic and NOT the noise floor

naming_retest.rule: the noise floor is the A-vs-B disagreement rate: same question, same option texts, same order, only the option-list labelling differs, so the answer should not change. Its one-sided 95% upper bound SETS the pass line of `mapping` (see `mapping.pass_line`, Plan r3 §10); it is not decoration.

mapping.naming_rule: a bare-letter reply is classified `letter_reply`, escalated ONCE with the block applied to the first two generated positions and an instruction not to write a letter, and either resolved by that retry (`resolved_by_escalation`) or recorded as `letter_reply_after_escalation` and counted unevaluable. The letter is never converted into option text.

pass_line.can_prove: a gross mis-wiring only: a fault that contradicts on a large share of the 48 pairs is rejected (the smallest detectable rate is reported)
pass_line.cannot_prove: that the letter<->option map is correct; a fault on a minority of pairs is invisible at 48 pairs

coverage.rule: e_max = the largest e with e <= B(n_pairs - e, p_hi) (C = 0, the most favourable case); a cell with more than e_max unevaluable pairs cannot pass at any contradiction count.  required_coverage_frac = (n_pairs - e_max)/n_pairs.  slack_b_minus_c = B - C is the distance from the line at the observed n_eval; it is NOT how many further unevaluable pairs this run could absorb, because B shrinks with each one.  That quantity is max_absorbable_unevaluable_pairs = the largest e' with C + e' <= B(n_pairs - e', p_hi); quote that one for 'how many more the run could take'.  (This replaces the field `margin_pairs`, whose definition was B - C while its prose claimed the absorbable count.)

pass_line.refusal_rule: a reply that normalises to one of REFUSAL_PHRASES is a refusal, not an unparseable answer: if the unit's own option list contains an option with that normalised text it names that option (refusal_matched_option) and the pair is judged; otherwise the pair stays unevaluable (refusal_no_option) and is charged as a worst-case contradiction. A refusal is never mapped onto a neighbouring option by meaning.
pass_line.rule: registered in Plan plan-single-frame-random-question-r3 §9-§10 (control C; it supersedes the r2 §5 line, and the r2 verdict on the same numbers is reported as r2_rule_status). A pair is judged by the same comparison as before: the option the letter points at must equal the option the model names in free text on that same order, never derived from the letter. What changed is the treatment of a pair that could not be judged: it is charged as a worst-case contradiction. pass iff C + e <= B and e <= e_max; fail iff C > B (the contradictions alone exceed the line); incomplete iff C <= B < C + e, or e > e_max (too little coverage: no verdict can be given and the cell does not report); not_discriminating iff no pair was parsed on both channels, or p_hi >= 0.35 (the naming step is too unstable to gate a map). B = quantile_0.95(Binomial(n_eval, p_hi)), p_hi = one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound on the naming test-retest rate on the same pairs, e_max = the largest e with e <= B(n_pairs - e, p_hi). B_strict is the same line at retest 0/n_pairs. A pass says no gross mis-wiring, never that the map is correct.

pass_line.why_the_line_changed: two after-the-fact corrections, both written down before the run that uses them. (1) r2's zero tolerance was withdrawn because the naming step disagrees with itself on 1 of 8 pairs on the same question, so a 48-pair cell passed at 0.0016 and the criterion could only ever withhold. (2) r2's coverage = 1 rule was withdrawn for the same reason one level up: one unit that refuses to name an option made the whole cell incomplete, and under the same 95% convention a coverage = 1 rule withholds about 99% of runs of this size whatever the map does. Unevaluable pairs are now charged as contradictions, which is never looser than the r2 line: at the same n_eval it demands C <= B - e, i.e. strictly fewer contradictions.

mapping.rule: THE CRITERION. For each unit and each option order, opts[idx(letter)] must equal the option the model names in free text on that same order, read from the naming ask and matched on normalised strings. Never derived from the letter. The PASS LINE is the one registered in Plan plan-single-frame-random-question-r3 §9-§10 and computed in `mapping_pass_line`: a pair that cannot be judged is charged as a worst-case contradiction, so pass iff C + e <= B (the contradiction count plus the unevaluable pairs does not exceed what the naming step's own test-retest rate can produce at 95%) and e <= e_max (the derived coverage floor); fail iff C > B; incomplete iff C <= B < C + e or e > e_max. A pass says 'no gross mis-wiring', never 'the map is correct'.
mapping.why_split: the r2 rule `n_text_preserved == n` measured the model's sensitivity to option order (5/6, 4/6, 2/3, 5/6; 0 of 4 cells passed) while 0 of 21 units carried the mapping-fault signature; it was withdrawn as an after-the-fact change and the corrected control re-run
mapping.why_the_line_changed: two after-the-fact corrections. (1) The line used to be zero contradictions; the naming step disagrees with itself on 1 of 8 pairs when only the option-list labelling changes, so a 48-pair cell passed at 0.0016 and the criterion could only ever withhold; it was replaced by the line derived from that same measured rate on the same pairs (r2 §5). (2) That line still demanded every pair evaluable, which made one refusing unit enough to withhold the cell; unevaluable pairs are now charged as worst-case contradictions and the coverage floor is derived from the same inequality (r3 §10). At e = 0 the two versions agree; at e > 0 r3 demands strictly fewer contradictions. The criterion, the pairs and the consequence (landing = null unless pass) are unchanged.

naming_block.computed_from: the tokenizer's own vocabulary: every id that decodes to a bare single Latin letter (any case, optionally wrapped in ()/[] and/or closed with . : ) -), plus the same check applied again at the second generated position when the first generated token is whitespace only
naming_block.what: those ids are suppressed at the first generated token of the naming ask only (and at the second position on the escalation retry), so the answer cannot be a bare letter. No option is favoured: only single-letter tokens are removed, and a letter that is itself an option's whole text is not removed for that unit (`blocking_conflicts_with_option`).
naming_block.why: v1 and v2 both got a bare letter back under two different instructions (task-bbb62d92f8, task-83b6aa08bc: 0 of 30 pairs evaluable each), and v3's hard-coded ids 32-36 (upper-case A-E only) were bypassed with lower-case d/c/b and out-of-range F/G/H/M (task-f0d4a231c4: 26 of 42 unevaluable)
